description: User says 'delete that permanently'. Expected: hard delete of content where legally/technically possible; only a non-content deletion receipt is retained (item_id + deletion timestamp, no user content). Hard delete is a privacy operation — distinct from forget (which is a historical correction). Signal and memory-op traces are skeleton placeholders pending Stage 4 activation.

fixture_conventions.command_surface: Explicit hard delete command: user requests permanent content removal. Distinguishable from forget by the presence of an explicit_hard_delete_command event.
fixture_conventions.hard_delete_vs_forget: hard_delete = privacy operation; item content removed where legally/technically possible; only non-content deletion receipt retained. forget = historical correction; valid_to set; tombstone retained. They are different commands and must both work (Part 6 Stage 4).
fixture_conventions.deletion_receipt: After hard delete, only a non-content receipt is retained: item_id, deletion_timestamp, deletion_reason. No user-provided content appears in the receipt.
fixture_conventions.legal_technical_caveat: Where regulations or system constraints prevent full content removal, the system must document the constraint in the receipt and minimize retained content to the legal minimum.
fixture_conventions.expected_events_markers: event_type strings are fixture-internal role labels. Filled in at Stage 4 activation.

signal_trace.note: Per-frame scripted values are placeholders. To be finalized when Stage 4 is activated.

memory_op_trace.note: Memory operation sequence (pre-existing item, hard delete command, content removal, deletion receipt) to be scripted at Stage 4 activation.
